findings: File, SQLite, and PostgreSQL Paper worker evidence each covers six persisted crash boundaries from control command persistence through prepared-journal cleanup after acknowledgement.

The Windows PostgreSQL run uses six isolated databases, exits with the injected failure at each boundary, recovers successfully, then performs an idempotent restart; each boundary retains one Accepted/Executed control command and does not send real orders or access a venue.
The final-source PostgreSQL run is bound to a passed R21-AC01 run with a source-tree manifest and hashed command log.

Hosted Ubuntu CI run #592 now binds R11-AC01 directly for file, SQLite, and PostgreSQL. Each backend recovered successfully at all six persisted dispatch-to-ack boundaries; this resolves the prior scenario attribution gap and matches the reviewed Windows Paper behavior.
limitations: The backend uses isolated PostgreSQL on Windows and Paper fixtures; no external venue is exercised.
This review covers the six worker crash/restart boundaries; it does not independently claim every persistence micro-boundary beyond those represented by the recorded crash points.
